In its quarterly earnings report, Apple revealed that R&D spending climbed to a record high of $11.73 billion, continuing the sharp acceleration trend seen throughout fiscal year 2026. Here are the details.

Apple Increases R&D Spending

Last quarter, Apple reported R&D spending of $11.4 billion, a 34% year-over-year increase.

On the company's earnings call, Tim Cook stated that Apple had "significantly increased investment," noting that R&D spending was growing "well above the company's overall level."

He reiterated that R&D spending was "expanding dramatically on a year-over-year basis," particularly when discussing Apple's AI investments. Apple's CFO Kevan Parekh added that AI-related spending was being layered on top of Apple's normal product roadmap investments in an incremental fashion.

Today, Apple reported its fiscal Q3 2026 results, with R&D spending reaching a record high of $11.73 billion, up 32% year-over-year, bringing Apple's total R&D spending for fiscal year 2026 to date to $34.04 billion.

For comparison, Apple's total R&D spending for the entire fiscal year 2025 was $34.55 billion. That means, with one quarter still remaining, the company's R&D spending for the current fiscal year has already approached last year's full-year total and has already surpassed the full-year R&D spending for fiscal years 2024 and 2023.

Over the past few days, Wall Street has harshly punished some companies that announced accelerated AI-related spending but failed to demonstrate equally clear short-term returns.

Alphabet's stock price fell 7% after the company raised its 2026 capital expenditure forecast by $15 billion, to a range of $195 billion to $205 billion. Meta's stock price also fell by approximately 9% to 10%, after the company raised the lower end of its full-year capital expenditure forecast to $130 billion while also reporting a 91% decline in free cash flow.

Apple's stock price is currently down approximately 4% in after-hours trading. This reaction could change during the earnings call later, and may shift again when the market officially opens tomorrow.
